title: Phosphoric acid-functionalized biochar derived from residual neem seed biomass after biodiesel production for adsorption of brilliant green and malachite green dyes from contaminated water
content: In this study, sorbents were produced and functionalized from the discarded residual biomass of the (Melia azadirachta) neem seeds (RMNSB) after biodiesel production. This biomass was selected because, during biodiesel production by transesterification and solvent washing operations, a huge amount of residual mass (∼80%) is generated, which is associated with secondary waste production. To achieve the zero-waste goal, the discarded biomass of neem seed was transformed into functionalized biochar, which has enhanced overall properties and sorption potential. The batch adsorption experiments for the simultaneous elimination of Brilliant Green (BG) and Malachite Green (MG) dyes from binary BG–MG solution wastewater were examined under varying parameters. Kinetic data demonstrated agreement with both the pseudo-first-order (R2 > 0.99) and pseudo-second-order models (R2 > 0.98) for the BG and MG dyes. Equilibrium data demonstrated good agreement with both the Langmuir (R2 > 0.99) and Freundlich (R2 > 0.99) isotherm models for the BG and MG dyes, which indicates the presence of simultaneous adsorption features depicted by both models. The specific surface area, sample density, pore volume, and pore diameter measured are approximately 49.5 m2 g−1, 1.00 g cm−3, 0.063 cm3 g−1, and 5.25 nm, respectively. Maximum adsorption capacity of BG and MG onto the bionanosorbent was recorded as 164.42 mg g−1 and 172.24 mg g−1, respectively. Analysis of other thermodynamic parameters confirmed the spontaneity and endothermic character of the adsorption of both dyes, with enhanced randomization at the interface between the bionanosorbent and solution. Further studies of the FRMNSB biochar samples were carried out utilizing Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy-Attenuated Total Reflectance (FTIR-ATR), Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Zeta Potential (ZP), and Simultaneous Thermal Analyzer (STA) analysis/techniques to provide a full understanding of the physicochemical, thermomechanical, and morpho-structural features.
